messages:
ada: seeing a 99th tail spike on us-west-2 inference pool. KV prefix hit-rate collapsed from ~84% -> 12% around 12:17 UTC, throughput dropped ~30% :grimacing:
ops-bot: alert: kv_hitrate_drop us-west-2 pool 12:18:02
jamal: rolling? any recent cfg changes?
ada: afaik a small runtime tweak shipped at 12:15 by @mike — changed kernel-selection fallback order + enabled 'adaptive_kernel_switch' in canary. logs show a lot of fallback kernels hitting slower code paths.
mike: yeh i flipped adaptive_kernel_switch=true for canary 12:15 as perf experiment. thought it would reduce kernel stalls. didn't expect mem blowups. reverting now.
sophia: can we get top prefixes that were evicted? sounds like prefix key thrashing or a TTL miscalc.
ada: dumping top evictions now. snippet:
```
EVICT prefix: tenant-42:conv:128 -> 230k evictions
EVICT prefix: tenant-17:prompt:seq -> 180k evictions
KV pool mem_used jump 78%-> 96% at 12:16
oom_killer: reclaimed 0 pages
```
jamal: that smells like cache poisoning / large prefix cardinality. Any noisy tenant spikes?
mike: checking metrics: tenant-42 had a burst of long-context requests at 12:10-12:20, avg seq_len 6k tokens. Batching heuristics may have aggregated and increased memory per request.
sophia: adaptive kernel switch might prefer a kernel variant that keeps larger kv-frames in RAM until eviction, increasing per-req mem. Also dynamic batching param changed? what was the config?
mike: I toggled 'enable_dynamic_batching=false' -> true for canary. rolling disabled burst cap. so batch sizes grew with seq length.
ada: reproduce plan: 1) revert adaptive_kernel_switch 2) cap batch size to 256 tokens/req 3) backfill prefix TTL bump for high-card prefixes
jamal: run flamegraph on expensive path pls. I think kernel fallback path is spending time in memcpy + lock contention.
ada: profile attached (s3/gcs link): flame: https://internal/snapshots/1887654321/flame.svg
sophia: quick grep of runtime logs shows many 'kv_get' latency 500-2000ms while cache hit would be <5ms. kvcache miss flood aligns with eviction.
ops-bot: deploy rollback started by @mike at 12:33 UTC
mike: rollback complete at 12:36. early signs: hit-rate back to 65%, p99 down to normal but still recovering.
ada: follow-ups: - add guardrail to dynamic batching that respects kv pool pressure - add eviction telemetry per-tenant - add automated TTL bump when eviction rate > X
sophia: also add a kernel selection canary that runs perf-sim on small subset vs real traffic before switching global default
jamal: file a postmortem and include perf profiles + heap snapshots. tag tenant-42 for rate-limiting in future
ada: thanks everyone. i'll open an RFC for adaptive_kernel_switch gating with kv pressure signals :thumbsup:
